title: OpenAI compatibility: canonical tool selector envelope and framed handoff semantics
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a canonical streaming 'tool_selector' envelope and clearer mapping rules from OpenAI-style function/tool schemas to Redwood tool manifests. Improves robustness of tool_choice handling during fragmented streams and provides an opt-in strict compatibility mode. Backwards-compatible by default.
description:
Motivation: clients integrating with OpenAI-style function/tool calling expect deterministic 'tool_choice' semantics and stable streaming handoffs when the assistant decides to invoke external tools. We observed multiple interoperability issues: (1) fragmented streaming messages lost tool selection context when the 'tool' metadata was embedded mid-stream, (2) schema mapping between OpenAI function objects and Redwood tool definitions produced loose/ambiguous typed outputs, and (3) fallbacks for partial/malformatted tool_choice messages were inconsistent across runtimes.

This PR implements a canonical 'tool_selector' envelope in the streaming protocol designed to be minimal and backwards-compatible. The envelope is emitted as a discrete framed event before tool invocation payloads; it contains a stable tool id, the resolved schema reference, and an explicit selection_reason (model_ranking | heuristic | user_request). When a client receives an early 'tool_selector' frame it can immediately prepare local tooling (e.g. open sockets, allocate cache partition) without waiting for the tool payload.

Key changes (summary): implements adapter and runtime plumbing to emit/consume the new envelope; adds deterministic mapping rules from OpenAI "function" schema to Redwood tool manifests (name, inputs.schema_v2, outputs.type_hints, required_fields); adds strict-mode toggle on the OpenAI compatibility adapter which rejects ambiguous tool_choice tokens instead of attempting best-effort mapping; updates streaming fragmentation boundaries so that partial JSON fragments don't change selector->payload association; extensive tests and new doc pages describing the behavior and migration.

Design notes: - Canonical envelope: {"type":"tool_selector","tool_id":"<id>","schema_ref":"<uri>","selection_reason":"..."} emitted as a single framed event in the stream. The framing ensures it won't be split across TCP buffers (runtime uses existing framed-message header). - Mapping rules: prefer explicit function.name -> tool_id; fall back to fuzzy matches derived from schema title and metadata. When multiple matches exist and strict_mode=true we return an ambiguity error to the client (400-level) so callers can disambiguate. - Streaming handoff: the runtime now pins the selector-to-stream id mapping for the lifetime of the invocation; subsequent fragments without a selector are attributed to the pinned tool until an explicit end_of_tool frame. - Backwards compatibility: when the upstream model sends the older 'tool_choice' token or in-stream text hint, the adapter performs the same mapping but emits a synthetic selector envelope before tool payload to make downstream processing uniform.

Testing and validation: unit tests for the mapping heuristics (tests/test_tool_mapping.py), integration tests that simulate fragmented streams (integration/streaming/test_tool_stream_fragments.py), and end-to-end compatibility tests against an OpenAI-compat client harness. CI showed a transient streaming e2e failure on the first run (flaky network ordering); reran and green. Performance impact: negligible (<1% latency) when selector envelope is emitted; small allocation decrease in runtimes that now reuse pinned metadata.

Migration: no action required for most customers. Opt-in strict_mode is exposed via the OpenAI adapter flag "compat_tool_strict=true" in the Redwood API shim. Customers who want to guarantee exact rejected/accepted mappings should enable strict mode and update their prompt/tool naming to match the canonical tool_id. See docs/openai-compat/tool-calling.md for examples and a migration checklist.

Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag: start in canary for 24h, enable for 20% traffic for 72h, then 100% if no regressions. Observability: added per-invocation metric openai.compat.selector_emitted and mapping.ambiguity.rate and dashboards in Redwood Console.

Related: ENG-2241 (compatibility follow-up), SUP-897 (customer report about partial tool_choice streams).

notes_for_release: This improves OpenAI function/tool calling compatibility and stream stability. Documented examples include a migration checklist and sample adapter config.
